question: Using Section 4I.06 and Figure 4I-4, describe the pedestrian interval order, minimum buffer interval, and walking speed normally used for clearance timing.
model_answer: Direct Answer: The pedestrian interval sequence is: walk interval (WALKING PERSON), followed immediately by the pedestrian change interval (flashing UPRAISED HAND, typically with countdown), followed by a buffer interval (steady UPRAISED HAND) of at least 2 seconds before conflicting traffic is released. The sum of the pedestrian change interval and buffer interval must be at least the calculated pedestrian clearance time. Clearance timing is normally based on a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second, with slower speeds considered where slower pedestrians or wheelchair users routinely cross, and 3 feet per second used to check the total of walk interval plus clearance time. Standards (mandatory): - "A pedestrian change interval consisting of a flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall begin immediately following the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication. Following the pedestrian change interval, a buffer interval consisting of a steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall be displayed for at least 2 seconds prior to the release of any conflicting vehicular movement. The sum of the time of the pedestrian change interval and the buffer interval shall not be less than the calculated pedestrian clearance time... The buffer interval shall not begin later than the beginning of the red clearance interval, if used." - Where the pedestrian clearance time is sufficient only for crossing to a median, "median-mounted pedestrian signals, with pedestrian detectors... shall be provided and signing such as the R10-3d sign... shall be provided to notify pedestrians to cross only to the median to await the next WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication." Guidance (recommended): - The pedestrian clearance time should be sufficient to allow a pedestrian who left the curb or edge of pavement at the end of the WALK indication to travel at a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second to at least the far side of the traveled way or to a median of sufficient width to wait. - Where pedestrians who walk slower than 3.5 feet per second, or pedestrians who use wheelchairs, routinely use the crosswalk, a walking speed of less than 3.5 feet per second should be considered. - The total of the walk interval and pedestrian clearance time should allow a pedestrian who left the pedestrian detector (or a point 6 feet behind the curb face/pavement edge) at the start of the WALK indication to travel at 3 feet per second to the far side of the traveled way (or the median in a two-stage crossing); any additional time needed should be added to the walk interval. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 4I-4 shows the interval order — steady WALK (7 seconds minimum), flashing UPRAISED HAND with countdown during the pedestrian change interval, then a steady UPRAISED HAND buffer interval of 2 seconds minimum — with the calculated pedestrian clearance time spanning the change interval and (optionally) the buffer, and the countdown "zero" point at the start of the buffer interval. [Image 2] Page 765 presents Figure 4I-4 in context with the footnotes noting the countdown display is optional for change intervals of 7 seconds or less and that the buffer interval shall always be provided and displayed. [Image 3] Page 764 states the Standard that the change interval begins immediately after the WALK indication, the buffer interval must last at least 2 seconds before release of conflicting traffic, and the sum of the change and buffer intervals must equal or exceed the calculated clearance time. [Image 4] Page 767 addresses related walk-interval timing where a leading pedestrian interval is used. [Image 5] Page 771 concerns pedestrian hybrid beacon operation and is not directly relevant to the interval order question. Citations: - Section 4I.06 Standard §4 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Standard §16 (p.725) - Section 4I.06 Guidance §7 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Guidance §10 (p.725) - Section 4I.06 Guidance §14 (p.725) - Figure 4I-4 (p.724) - Page 765 - Page 764
gold_answer: The order is WALK, flashing DONT WALK pedestrian change interval, then steady DONT WALK buffer interval. The buffer interval is at least 2 seconds before conflicting traffic is released, and clearance is normally evaluated using 3.5 feet per second.
